faq.title: Veelgestelde Vragen
faq.q4: Does the tool work with transparent PNGs?
faq.a4: Yes. If you click on a transparent area, the tool will typically return the color of the underlying canvas (usually white or checkered).
faq.q5: Is there a limit on the number of colors I can pick?
faq.a5: No, you can pick as many colors as you need. There are no limits or restrictions on our free online tool.
faq.q6: Why would I use HSL instead of HEX?
faq.a6: HSL is more intuitive for adjusting colors (e.g., making a color 10% darker), while HEX is just a computer code that is hard to read for humans.
faq.q7: Is this tool safe for company logos?
faq.a7: Absolutely. Because your image stays in your browser and is never uploaded to our servers, your sensitive company assets remain private.
faq.q8: Does the tool work on iPhones and iPads?
faq.a8: Yes, our tool is fully responsive and uses touch events to allow color picking on mobile devices.
faq.q9: Can I save my color palette for later?
faq.a9: The history list is available during your current session. We recommend copying the HEX codes into a document for long-term storage.
faq.q10: What does a 'pixel' actually represent in color terms?
faq.a10: A pixel is the smallest unit of a digital image. In a standard image, it's a single color value composed of Red, Green, and Blue light data.

intro.title: Mastering Your Palette: The Definitive Guide to Online Image Color Extraction
intro.subtitle: Bridge the gap between inspiration and implementation with our pixel-perfect color picker.
intro.p1: Every great design starts with a spark of inspiration, and often, that inspiration comes from the colors we see in the world around us—a sunset, a vintage poster, or a stunning piece of modern digital art. However, identifying the exact digital signature of those colors has historically required expensive design software or clunky browser extensions. Our Image Color Picker is designed to simplify this process, giving you a professional-grade eyedropper tool that works directly in your web browser, allowing you to extract HEX, RGB, and HSL codes with surgical precision.
intro.p2: In the world of web development and UI/UX design, consistency is everything. A single shade of blue that is slightly 'off' can break a brand's visual identity. Our tool empowers you to upload any image—whether it's a high-resolution photograph, a logo file, or a screenshot of a competitor's website—and find the exact color values used. We've built in a high-magnification zoom feature that lets you navigate individual pixels, ensuring that you don't just get 'a' color, but 'the' color you were looking for.
intro.p3: Beyond simple extraction, our tool is built for a fast-paced creative workflow. We provide color values in multiple formats (HEX, RGB, and HSL) so you can copy and paste them directly into your CSS files, design mockups, or brand guidelines. It's a frictionless way to build a professional color palette from any source, completely free and without the need for an account.

story.title: The Science of Color Picking: From Pixels to Design Systems
story.p1: To appreciate the power of an image color picker, it's helpful to understand how computers represent color. Most digital images use the RGB (Red, Green, Blue) model, where each pixel is assigned a value for each color channel. When you use our 'eyedropper' tool, you are essentially querying the underlying data array of the image to find the exact numerical values for a specific coordinate. This raw data is then converted into different human-readable formats like HEX or HSL.
story.p2: HEX (Hexadecimal) is the language of the web. It's a six-character code like #3498db that browsers use to render colors. While developers love HEX for its brevity, designers often prefer HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) because it's more 'intuitive.' If you want to make a color slightly lighter or less vibrant, adjusting the HSL values is much easier than doing the math for a HEX string. Our tool provides both, ensuring that every member of a creative team has the data they need.
story.p3: One of the biggest challenges in color extraction is sub-pixel anti-aliasing. In many images, the edges of objects are 'blurred' by the computer to make them look smooth. This means that if you click on the very edge of a logo, you might get a mixture of the logo color and the background color. Our built-in magnifier tool is essential here, allowing you to see exactly which pixel your cursor is over, avoiding the 'muddy' colors that often result from imprecise selection.
story.p4: Branding and Identity are perhaps the most common use cases for our tool. Professional brand kits often lose their original documentation over time. If you're a new designer tasked with creating a flyer for a company, you can simply upload their existing logo to our tool and instantly recover their exact 'Brand Blue' or 'Logo Red.' It's an essential utility for maintaining visual continuity across different platforms and media types.
story.p5: Web Accessibility is another critical area where our color picker shines. To meet WCAG standards, text must have a certain contrast ratio against its background. Designers use our tool to pick the background color from a hero image and then use those HEX codes in a contrast checker to ensure their typography remains legible for users with vision impairments. It's about being both creative and responsible.
story.p6: Consider the inspiration phase of a project. Many designers keep 'mood boards' or 'swipe files.' By using our color picker on your inspiration gallery, you can build a cohesive color scheme for a new website in minutes. You can extract the dominant tones and the subtle accent colors, creating a palette that is grounded in real-world aesthetics rather than just random color spectrum selections.
story.p7: Security is a high priority for our users. Design drafts and internal assets are often sensitive. Because our Image Color Picker processes your images locally in your browser using the HTML5 Canvas API, your images are never actually sent to our servers. This ensures 100% privacy—your designs never leave your machine, and your creative secrets stay your own.
story.p8: In conclusion, a color picker is more than just a tool; it's the glue that binds inspiration to implementation. Whether you're a seasoned developer or a first-time designer, use our Image Color Picker to take the guesswork out of your color workflow. It's precise, it's fast, and it's designed to make your creative life easier.
